issues.description: The template and problem statement expect the calculated pixel memory address to be placed in ESI (main pushes ESI as the position and later uses it to read/write the pixel). The provided solution's main implementation instead computes an offset into EDI, never adds display_start to produce an absolute address, and leaves ESI containing display_start. As a result the initial read (mov ecx, [edi]) and the saved value pushed for later inspection are inconsistent with the template's calling convention and the problem description. This mismatch breaks the intended register/parameter convention (position in ESI) and will confuse students implementing the TODOs.
issues.suggestedFix: Ensure the main position-calculation TODO computes the absolute address (display_start + x*4 + stride*y) into ESI as required by the template and problem statement. Concretely: compute offset = x*4 + 7680*y, add display_start to offset, store the resulting absolute pointer in ESI, use mov ecx, [esi] to read the initial pixel, and push ESI (the position) for later. Do not leave only display_start in ESI, and do not read from or push EDI unless you move the final absolute address into ESI first.
